I assumed the submission was wrong and went looking. Most of it held up under independent recomputation — but the load-bearing control has a real flaw.

## What held up

I rebuilt both tables from the raw pickles through my own code path (no `make_tables.py`): **all 13×8 cells of Table 1, all 6×8 of Table 2, the noise floor, and every headline delta match to 4 dp.** I also recomputed the argmax of every column and confirmed all 20 bolded cells are genuine maxima.

I wrote my own sampler test rather than trusting `test_sampler.py`: across all three schemas from both user and artist starts, **0 non-edges and 0 type violations**; walk totals (152,930 / 148,000 / 148,000) exactly match the log; rare-artist sampling is empirically 1/deg(a) to 4×10⁻⁴.

A nice independent cross-check fell out: the type-blind run made 154,470 walks ⟹ 19 isolated nodes in H, and 666 − 647 = 19 — two unrelated artefacts agreeing on the cold-start coverage claim.

R7 done myself (page text, page render, and `page_011_fig_02.jpeg` at native resolution — illustrative only, nothing to transcribe). p1 reuse is byte-identical, and I checked the one thing that could have voided it: p1's `impl.py` was edited *after* its results were saved, but that edit was comment-only. Figures are vector, legible, data-driven. Compiles clean, lint clean, R5 clean.

## What I found

**[1.1, major] The budget-matched control is matched by walk *count*, not corpus size.**

| config | walks | tokens | walks reaching len 40 |
|---|---|---|---|
| control DeepWalk ×22 | 153,076 | 6,123,040 | 100% |
| metapath U-A-U | 152,930 | 6,117,200 | 100% |
| metapath U-U-A-U | 148,000 | 3,593,757 | **32.2%** |
| metapath U-U-U-A-U | 148,000 | 4,068,117 | **43.7%** |

"Matching the Task-4 corpus to within 0.1%" is true for three configs and **wrong by a third for U-U-U-A-U — the row the control exists to adjudicate.** The headline "−0.0016, i.e. nothing" is measured against a control handed ~50% more training tokens.

The evidence was already in the worker's own log: Skip-Gram time drops 111s → 65s/72s, ratios 0.59/0.65, matching the token ratios 0.587/0.665 almost exactly. gensim time tracks tokens, not walks.

**[1.2, major]** The write-up documents only *first-step* failure, but walks also dead-end mid-way (mean lengths 24.3 and 27.5, not 40) — mostly when an A→U step lands on a socially isolated user. Correct implementation, undisclosed behaviour.

Plus four minors (walk-count inconsistency at line 118, the 204.5→205 rounding, an unused label/package, and length). Neither major requires re-running anything — no reported measurement is wrong, but a load-bearing methodological claim is inaccurate and the aggregate-null conclusion is conservative in a direction the reader isn't told about.

Checklist written to `validators/p2/checklist.md`.

VERDICT: FAIL
